title: Subcomplex — face-closed subset of cells
body_html:
Subcomplex

A cellular subcomplex is a face-closed subset of the cells of $X$. Modelled after mathlib's Subgroup / Submonoid idiom.

Signature

lean structure Subcomplex (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] where carrier : Set X face_closed' : ∀ {E F : X}, E ≤ F → F ∈ carrier → E ∈ carrier

  • carrier: the underlying set of cells in $S \subseteq [\![X]\!]$;
  • face_closed': closed under taking faces — if a cell is in $S$, so is every cell below it in the face poset.

SetLike

lean instance : SetLike (Subcomplex X) X where coe S := S.carrier coe_injective' := fun S T h => by cases S; cases T; congr

This gives $E \in S$ notation and coercion to Set X, matching how Subgroup G is used in mathlib.

User-facing face_closed

The primed field is the raw structure axiom. A user-facing form using $\in$ is exposed separately:

lean theorem face_closed (S : Subcomplex X) {E F : X} (hEF : E ≤ F) (hF : F ∈ S) : E ∈ S := S.face_closed' hEF hF

Downstream uses

  • Setwise stabiliser Quasi-fundamental domain takes a Subcomplex as input.
  • The image of the induction embedding CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X' (Prop 2.8) is packaged as a Subcomplex.ofIota d on the induced space.
  • Face-closedness of the QFD subcomplex is crucial for the reverse direction Reverse-direction induction: reconstructing X as G ×^P S from a QFD.
